text:
nadia: Heads up — after the continuous-batcher heuristic tweak rolled last night we're seeing a P99 tail spike on some fleets. p50 is unchanged but p99 jumped ~120ms -> ~680ms and overall throughput down ~18% for small-req workloads.

perf-bot: [ALERT] anomaly detected on cont-batcher-v2 at 2422140000: p99 latency > 500ms for model=redwood-open-7b, seq=<=64.

sam: Which canary/cluster is impacted? any kernels switched recently?

nadia: Canary id canary-17 on us-west-2, node group cg-small. The heuristic change was the token budget target reduction + smaller min_join_ms. It was intended to favor lower latency but seems to create weird microbatch shape churn.

kevin: Quick numbers from traces: prefix cache miss rate jumped from 2% -> 19% on the affected nodes, KV eviction rate doubled. Kernel affinity flips/sec increased ~6x.

tess: Oof. That sounds like more kernel thrash + KV thrash for short requests. Can we see the exact config diff?

nadia: Pasted the relevant diff from the rollout config:

```
{"batching": {"token_budget_target": 1200, "min_join_ms": 1, "enable_conservative_affinity": false}}
```

Previous (prod) was token_budget_target=4000, min_join_ms=3, enable_conservative_affinity=true.

sam: So smaller token_budget + lower join latency -> more tiny batches, more kernel switches, more KV churn. That matches the symptom set. Any flamegraphs / kernel occupancy?

kevin: Ran a short profiling window:
- kernel_switches/sec: 42 -> 260
- microbatch_coalesce_rate: 82% -> 31%
- avg_batch_size_tokens: 2100 -> 680
- prefix_cache_hit: 0.98 -> 0.81

kevin: Also attached a tiny snippet from the runtime log:
```
[2024-11-08T03:12:41Z] batcher: formed microbatch size=2 tokens=46 target_kernel=small, previous_kernel=large, switched=true
[2024-11-08T03:12:41Z] kvcache: evict candidate=prefix:abc, reason=cache_pressure
```
tess: Can we try a conservative hotfix: revert token_budget_target to 4000 but keep the new min_join_ms? That should reduce tiny-batch formation quickly. Or enable conservative kernel affinity restore.

sam: Agreed. If we revert token_budget_target we should also flip on conservative_affinity to avoid rapid kernel flipping while we observe.

infra-bot: Note: rollback window open. Canary rollback scheduled in 30m unless acknowledged.

nadia: I'm going to roll a targeted hotfix to canary-17 now: set token_budget_target=4000 and enable_conservative_affinity=true. Will monitor p99 and cache hit rates.

kevin: If hotfix applied, also add a short-term metric alert for kernel_switches/sec > 100 to avoid re-blast.

nadia: Hotfix applied to canary-17 at 2422203450. Running quick smoke:
```
curl -sS https://canary-17.metrics/api/latency?model=redwood-open-7b&seq=32 | jq .p99
> 132
```

perf-bot: [RESOLVED] anomaly on cont-batcher-v2 cleared at 2422203500. p99 returned to baseline on the canary.

nadia: Canary looks good; prefix_cache_hit back up to ~96%, throughput recovering. I'll promote the hotfix to the rest of the cg-small nodes and schedule a follow-up to tune token_budget_target more conservatively (maybe 2800) and add a kernel_affinity backoff.

sam: Thanks — please add a short runbook entry for this flip (what config to roll back and a quick check list). Also add test that simulates microburst small-req mixes so our heuristic doesn't overshoot.

kevin: I'll prepare a perf test harness that can run workloads with variable short/long ratio and assert kernel_switches/sec stays under threshold.

nadia: Great. Monitoring for 30m then I'll close. If anyone sees anything odd ping here. :thumbsup:
